items.prompt: BFS level-order traversal uses a queue because?
choices: Nodes discovered earlier must expand before later ones
BFS forbids revisiting with a set
items.whyRight: FIFO expands in discovery order, which equals hop distance on unweighted graphs.
whyWrong: The queue does not sort; the visit order creates distances.
A visited set is separate from the fringe structure.

items.prompt: A deque differs from a plain queue by allowing?
items.whyRight: Double-ended queues support both ends without becoming a free middle splice API.
whyWrong: Middle indexing is still not the deque contract.
Stack-only would drop the front end.

items.prompt: Implement a queue with two stacks. Amortized dequeue is O(1) because?
choices: Each element moves at most twice between stacks
You scan the longer stack each time
items.whyRight: Pouring from in-stack to out-stack happens rarely per element.
whyWrong: Scanning would be linear each call.

items.prompt: Sliding-window maximum with a deque stores indices that are?
choices: Candidates still inside the window, in decreasing value order
Sorted by index only with no value rule
items.whyRight: Front is the max; back pops smaller useless candidates.
whyWrong: Keeping everything wastes space and breaks O(n).
Index order alone does not yield the max.
Sampling is approximate, not the classic algorithm.

items.prompt: When is a queue the wrong first tool?
choices: You need the most recently deferred item first (undo)
You need fair processing of arrival order
You buffer tasks for a worker pool
